parole.significato: A Sumerian 'house of tablets', a place of learning where archives and literature were stored on clay tablets. A school…
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Sumerian 𒂍𒁾𒁀𒀀 (e₂-dub-ba-a /⁠edubak⁠/, “school”, literally “house of tablets”).

parole.significato: A Sumerian title designating the ruler or prince of a city state.
A member of an androgynous class of priests of the Sumerian goddess Inanna.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Sumerian 𒍑𒆪 (gala), related to Akkadian 𒍑𒆪 (kalû). A connection to the similar Phrygian and Roman priests of Cybele called gallae or galli has been suggested, but evidence is lacking.

parole.significato: A member of the Guti people.
A kind of equid in ancient Mesopotamia (probably a donkey-onager cross).
A ruler of a city state in ancient Sumer.
parole.testo: Learned borrowing from Sumerian 𒈗 (lugal, “king, lord”).

parole.significato: A type of ancient Sumerian carved oval or ovoid ornamental stone.
A person belonging to the ancient culture of Subartu.
parole.testo: From Sumerian 𒋢𒂔𒆠 (SU.BIR₄ᵏⁱ), Sumerian 𒋚 (Šubur/Subur); + -ian. See Subartu.
